steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Media regulation involves rules and systems that govern what media content can be produced, distributed, and accessed. It aims to protect audiences while preserving freedom of expression. | Key Fact: Ofcom regulates UK broadcasting — setting content standards, protecting audiences from harmful material, ensuring due impartiality in news, and managing the radio/TV spectrum. | Key Fact: The BBFC classifies films and some video content (U, PG, 12A, 12, 15, 18). Classification considers discrimination, drugs, horror, imitable behaviour, language, nudity, sex, threat, and violence. | Key Fact: IPSO (Independent Press Standards Organisation) regulates most UK newspapers and magazines. It handles complaints and enforces the Editors' Code of Practice, but has been criticised as weak.
